text:
kevin: Quick FYI — ran a focused nsys trace on the 512/64 batch path after yesterday's kernel-selector change. Seeing a weird 6-10ms spike in the KV-prefetch span for some requests.

maria: Can you paste the nvtx spans you used? Might be a naming collision making ranges merge.

kevin: Sure — current annotations: `NVTX_RANGE("request")`, `NVTX_RANGE("kv_prefetch")`, `NVTX_RANGE("kernel_dispatch")`, and `NVTX_PUSH("batch_window")`. Thinking to add request-id suffix like `kv_prefetch:req-<id>` so traces per-request don't unify.

bryan: +1 on per-request suffixes. But watch trace explosion in perfetto UI — adding full request ids kills readability. Maybe use `kv_prefetch:shard-<shard>` or `kv_prefetch:seqlen-<len>` as intermediate.

nishant: Can we instead add attributes/tags to the NVTX ranges rather than unique names? Perf tools show attributes in detail but preserve grouping. With NVTX we can push an id in `nvtxRangePushEx` payload.

kevin: Good call. I tried `nvtxRangePushEx(&attr)` with an int64 user data = request_id; perfetto shows it, but our trace post-processing script currently groups by range name only. We need to update the trace parser.

perf-bot: nsys run summary (kernel timeline snippets) attached:
```
Time window: 2026-02-28T14:12:03Z
Total tokens processed: 123k
Top kernels by self-time: attention_fwd (42%), matmul_1 (18%), kv_prefetch_cuda (12%)
Notable: kv_prefetch_cuda shows jitter 8.2ms p95 vs p50 1.6ms
```

maria: That jitter matches my local repro. It correlates with occasional CPU-side stall before launching prefetch kernel. Might be batching heuristic mis-grouping small requests and causing extra memcpy.

kevin: I attached the nvtx range timeline snapshot: `request -> batch_window -> kv_prefetch -> kernel_dispatch`. The problematic traces have an additional `cpu_spin` micro-range between batch_window and kv_prefetch.

bryan: Could you paste the small snippet of code where batching decides prefetch ordering? Maybe the heuristic applies a sleep/flush for cold caches.

kevin: snippet:
```
if (batch.size() < min_batch && now - last_send < batch_timeout) {
  // hold for more records
  continue;
}
// we emit NVTX before prefetch
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("kv_prefetch");
launch_kv_prefetch(batch);
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```
Edge case: `batch_timeout` is dynamic; occasionally a late wakeup causes the path to schedule immediate prefetch on main thread instead of worker pool. That explains CPU stall.

nishant: So two mitigations: 1) move prefetch launch off main thread always (worker pool), 2) mark prefetch NVTX as `async`/`external` so kernel timing is associated to device kernel instead of host hold. NVTX has `nvtxRangeCreateA` with attributes `NVTX_CATEGORY` and `NVTX_DOMAIN`. Could help.

maria: Also propose a naming convention doc: short base name + 1-2 machine tags. Example: `kv_pf|k:v1|b:512|s:sh2` where `kv_pf` is canonical, k=model kernel family, b=batch, s=shard. Keep total <32 chars to avoid UI truncation.

kevin: Love that. Less noise. I'll update the injector to write compressed labels and add `nvtxRangePushEx` user data with request fingerprint. Parser will still group by canonical label and can filter by fingerprint.

perf-bot: I pushed an automated diff to `perf/trace-parsers` with a basic parser change to read `user_data` from NVTX ranges. CI trace tests failing in one case (huge user_data values).

bryan: Make sure user_data is a 64-bit hash not the full GUID — store `xxhash64(request_id)` to avoid huge values.

kevin: Will do. Also thinking of adding a special range `kv_prefetch:cancel` for aborted prefetches so we can later filter those in dashboards.

maria: One more request: can we add a short log line to the runtime when prefetch takes >4ms: `WARN prefetch_latency=%d batch=%d kernel=%s` — will help tie traces to logs.

kevin: Added TODO in my branch. I'll run another nsys with async NVTX attrs + user_data hash and post screenshots. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 

trace-bot: Uploaded perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (kv_prefetch hotspots highlighted)
